item.text: {"text":"Multi-negative training is a strong candidate, but negative count and loss calibration should be tested separately. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies overconfidence from sampled BCE and combines more negatives with generalized BCE. Sampled softmax provides another efficient objective. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional sampling correction mishandles the always-present positive; its refined formulation reports improvements over standard logQ correction. This matters particularly for popularity-biased in-batch negatives; sampling correction does not itself resolve false negatives.\n\nAdaptive mining should balance informativeness against false-negative risk. [CATS (2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) combines item clustering with Thompson sampling, progressively reducing sampling from the positive item’s cluster while exploring neighboring clusters and the remaining catalog. Its cluster-based false-negative assumption is a heuristic, not an observed label. Practical RecHarness experiment proposal: compare uniform multi-negative sampled softmax and gBCE first, then add a small stochastic hard-negative component mined from a bounded candidate pool after warm-up. Exclude padding, the target, and known training positives; retain random negatives and avoid hardest-only selection. Sweep modest negative counts, such as 16/64/128, and hard-negative fractions under equal GPU budgets. These settings are proposed ablations, not published optima. Select using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; inspect Electronics margins and category regressions without assuming published gains transfer to this benchmark."}
